title: Celebrating the Lives of DJ DRocc and Morty

body_markdown:
**NAPLES, Fla. — Nov. 17, 2026** — Some of the people who make radio special become just as much a part of our lives as the stations themselves. Sherman “DJ DRocc” Howze and Christopher “Morty” Sampaio were those kinds of people. As Beasley Media Group mourns their passing, we remember what they brought to the airwaves—and what it meant to work alongside them.


For nearly two decades, DRocc helped shape radio in Fayetteville, North Carolina. As Urban Brand Manager and Program Director for WZFX (Foxy 99) and WUKS (107.7 The Bounce), he understood his listeners and helped fellow broadcasters find their footing. He could command attention as a DJ and mixer, but his coworkers’ recent


[tribute](https://www.facebook.com/foxy991/posts/pfbid0uUMdboP1GAfP1jfLaM9ghFDn5iz2ivPFpVyCpouDhcpnR1seGnc5jyJBfnDvtoSUl) says something more personal: As gifted as he was at his work, they loved him most for who he was.


They called him “Big Teddy Bear.” That affectionate nickname captures something a résumé never could—the warmth that made him such a central part of their lives.


Morty found his way into radio at 18 in Hawaii. That early start grew into a career spanning decades, including his years as the longtime producer of the KKLZ Morning Show in Las Vegas. Listeners knew his voice and humor. Coworkers knew the person helping bring each broadcast to life. His induction into the Nevada Broadcasters Hall of Fame in 2024 gave the industry an opportunity to celebrate a career that meant so much to him.


Our hearts are with their families and friends, especially our coworkers in Fayetteville and Las Vegas, where their absence is deeply felt.
